prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1057; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a rear-end collision in League City, Texas, where Driver 2's vehicle struck the rear of Driver 1's vehicle while both were traveling in the same lane. Driver 1 reported pain in the left shoulder and said the impact jolted them forward against the seatbelt. A Passenger was seated in the vehicle at the time and was present during the collision. Driver 2 described the event the same way Driver 1 did, and two independent witnesses at the scene gave statements consistent with that account. Photographs taken at the scene show rear-end damage to Driver 1's vehicle. Several small scratches on the rear bumper appear weathered and may predate this crash, and officers could not determine from the scene alone whether all of the visible damage resulted from this impact. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy shown in the exchanged insurance information. Driver 1 was transported for evaluation and released later that day. No citations were issued at the scene.
